Definition: of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively):--legion.
BiblicalUsage: legeṓn means a legion — rare in the text, and exact where it appears. In Mark 5:9, "My name [is] Legion: for we are many."; and in Luke 8:30, "Legion: because many devils were entered into him.". In Matthew 26:53, "and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a legion of demons is still only one word from Jesus away from the pigs and the deep — their number is their boast, and it means nothing to Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
